evidence.finding: Mean offered calls increased 60.7%, from 74.0 before the incident to 118.9 during/after it.
Volume was 48.1% above forecast at incident onset and remained 24.4%–72.2% above forecast for the rest of the window.
Mean service level fell from 90.85% before the incident to 54.33% during/after it, while ASA increased from 24.78 to 72.50 seconds.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant at 49; productive staffing did not decline, while occupancy increased from 68.1% to 98.9%.
All four queues experienced 49%–66% volume growth and 27%–43% service-level deterioration with unchanged queue staffing.
No routing, platform, or other operational event was recorded in the full visible window.

primary_root_cause_detail: An unexpected, center-wide demand surge began at 09:15. Offered volume remained 24.4%–72.2% above forecast, saturating otherwise stable staffing and causing service-level deterioration across all queues.
recommended_actions: Activate intraday surge staffing or cross-skilled overflow when actual demand materially exceeds forecast.
Configure real-time alerts for sustained actual-versus-forecast volume variance and occupancy approaching saturation.
Review the source of the 09:15 demand increase and incorporate any repeatable driver into forecasting and contingency plans.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Logged-in staffing remained at 49, productive staffing slightly increased, and adherence improved after incident onset.
Center AHT was essentially unchanged and averaged 0.24% below forecast during/after the incident.
Transfer rates were stable, degradation affected every queue, and no routing-change event was recorded.
No platform event was recorded, and the operational pattern is explained by above-forecast demand saturating stable capacity.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level incident was most likely caused by an unexpected center-wide demand surge beginning at 09:15, not by staffing loss, higher handle time, routing changes, or a platform incident. Stable capacity became saturated as volume substantially exceeded forecast across all queues.
